full_judgment:
M Enayetur Rahim J : On an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, this rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the proceedings in Special Case No. 2 of 2008 under sections 26(2) and 27(1) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 read with Rule 15gha(5) of the Emergency Powers Rules, 2007, now pending in the Court of Special Judge, Court No. 8, Dhaka so far as it relates to the accused petitioner should not be quashed and or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may deem Fit and proper. 

 2. Md Moniruzzaman Khan, a Deputy Director of Anti-Corruption commission, on 18-12-2007 lodged a First Information Report (hereinafter referred to as FIR) with Ramna Model Police Station implicating the present accused petitioner and his wife alleging inter-alia that the Commission on 5-7-2007 served a notice upon the accused petitioner through the Senior Jail Supper, Dhaka Central Jail to submit his wealth statements. Pursuant to the said notice the accused petitioner on 25-7-2007 submitted his wealth statements to the Commission. The Commission after scrutiny of the said wealth statements found that accused Altaf Hossain concealed his wealth amounting of Taka 55,60,248 and in fact he acquired Taka 1,59,52,367 which is disproportionate to his known-source of income. On the basis of the said FIR Ramna Police Station Case No. 67 dated 18-12-2007 under sections 26(2) and 27(1) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 (hereinafter referred to as Act of 2004) read with Emergency Powers Rules, 2007 was started. 

 4. Eventually, the case record was at first transmitted to the Metropolitan Senior Special Judge, Dhaka wherein it was numbered as Metro. Special Case No. 87 of 2008 and there-after, the case record again transferred to the Special Judge, Court No. 8, Dhaka wherein it was renumbered as Special Case No. 2 of 2008. 

 7. Mr Moudud Ahmed, the learned Advocate, appearing for the accused petitioner at the very outset candidly submits that he will not argue on the merit of the case. Referring to section 22 of the Act of 2004 as well as Rule 8 and 11 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007 (hereinafter referred to as the Rules of 2007) Mr Ahmed submits that it is the mandatory provision of law that an accused should be notified to submit oral or written statements within the time specified in the notice before lodging the FIR or submitting charge-sheet, as the case may be. But in the instant case no such notice was served either before the lodging of the First Information Report or before submitting charge-sheet and, as such, the statutory right of the accused to defend himself has been denied and thereby, the accused has been prejudiced seriously. He further submits that if the accused was given an opportunity to explain his position at the stage of inquiry or investigation the result of the investigation could have been otherwise. The Commission on violating the mandatory provision of law conducted the inquiry and submitted charge-sheet which is absolutely illegal in the eye of law and on the basis of said charge-sheet the continuation of the case is a sheer abuse of the process of the court. 

 8. Mr Md Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned Advocate, appearing for the Anti-Corruption Commission on refuting the above submissions of Mr Ahmed submits that the above provisions of law are not mandatory. It is the discretion of the Commission or the concerned investigating officer to notify the concerned person during inquiry or investigation if it appears to be at all necessary for the sake of inquiry or investigation. In this particular case the commission asked the accused petitioner to submit his statement of wealth and accordingly, he submitted the same. In view of that, it was not at all necessary to hear him regarding his wealth statement sub-mitted to the Commission. 

 9. Heard the learned Advocates for the parties, perused the relevant provisions of law as well as the rules and also go through an unreported judgment passed by a Division Bench of this Court in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 13124 of 2009 heard along with another Miscellaneous Case as placed by Mr Khan. 

 12. On perusal of the judgment passed in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 13124 of 2009 it transpires that Mr Ahmed was a party to the said case and he made similar submissions alike the present one. 

 13. It appears from the case under reference that a Division Bench of this Court upon examining Rule 8 and 11 of Rules, 2007 has observed as follows: 

 Apart from the point that no consequence affecting the proceeding is provided in the above quoted rules, use of the words "যদি মনে করে " and "সুযোগ প্রদান করিতে পারিবে" therein further makes it clear that service of notice upon the suspect/accused for hearing him about the allegation is not mandatory in each and every case. If the Enquiring/Investigating Officer even without hearing the person is prima facie satisfied about commission of the offence, he would go for lodgment of the FIR or submission of charge-sheet as the case may be. Admittedly the petitioner Md Zafrul Hasan furnished the statement of assets through his agent. The charge-sheet (annexure-B) shows that during investigation a statement in his defense was taken. The question of giving him no opportunity of being heard, therefore, does also not arise." 

 16. In the case of Habibur Rahman Mollah vs State, reported in 61 DLR (AD) 1, it has been held that: 

 In this connection, we must quote the following observations made by the Apex Court of India in a case of State of HP vs Lekh Raj, reported in 2000 SCC (Crl) 147. 

 21. The trial court is directed to proceed with the case in accordance with law. 

 24. The trial Court is directed to conclude the trial of the case within a period of 6 (six) months from the date of receipt of this judgment and order.
